items.title: AST SpaceMobile Stock Gets FCC Approval for Direct to Device Service
items.summary: AST SpaceMobile secured FCC approval for direct-to-device satellite service and outlined plans for intermittent nationwide coverage by late 2026 across key markets including the US, Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the UK. The combination of regulatory clearance and rollout plans, backed by partnerships with AT&T and Verizon, puts greater attention on AST SpaceMobile’s execution, capital use and timeline risk in building a usable space-based cellular network. items.title: Starlink’s 40x Upgrade Targets 150Mbps to Phones. AST SpaceMobile Has a Big Problem
items.summary: Key TakeawaysElon Musk said on Nov. 18 that SpaceX’s next direct-to-cell satellites start launching next year with 40x today’s bandwidth, and SpaceX aims for peak speeds of 150Mbps per user.

items.title: Forget AT&T and Verizon: Crown Castle Has More to Lose From Starlink’s 40x Upgrade
items.summary: Key TakeawaysElon Musk said SpaceX’s next direct-to-cell satellites will have 40x the bandwidth of today’s, and that AT&T and Verizon may lose some revenue. Crown Castle has more at stake than either carrier, since AT&T and Verizon pay 51% of its tower rent.
